summary.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). Management said the Gulf conflict pushed ATF prices up sharply and labour costs rose, and volume growth slowed to 4% YoY in Q4 after March.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; management said surface margin should improve with diesel-linked price pass-through, citing about 30% arbitrage. Surface grew in single digits in the last two quarters, with mid-single-digit to ~10% growth expected going forward.

segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.
Mumbai and Kolkata sorting centres moved to 5-year leases, which added ROU assets and raised depreciation.
Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Management said diesel rose about INR 8 and the company is passing it on to customers, with 85% pass-through expected and 10% to 15% of customers still negotiating.
Air fuel (ATF) rose about 50% and international air rates went up 2x to 3x after the Gulf conflict began at end-February, leading customers to hold shipments in March.
Labour costs rose 15% to 20%, adding about 100 basis points to overall cost, per management.
SME share of revenue was 48% to 52% against a historical 50:50 split; management expects a return to 50%+ with the last two months' results described as good.
Revenue per kg is about INR 12.3 to 12.4 with EBITDA of about INR 1.25 to 1.27 per kg, against a historical INR 1.8 to 2.0 per kg, per an analyst's calculation.
The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of about 10% to 11% and revenue growth of about 15% for FY27, with Q1 at high single digits and QoQ improvement after that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the multimodal segment margin dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air margins were temporarily hit by costs. Rail and C2C margins are stable and surface margin should improve with diesel pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the depreciation and interest increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Two sorting centres were moved to 5-year leases under Ind AS 116, which lifted ROU assets. Management said depreciation runs at about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA would have been about INR 29 crore, versus INR 32 crore reported, per the analyst's calculation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is about 2.5% of business, targeted to 5%, through D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse flows with SMEs and some aggregator platforms. Quick commerce is not in the strategy.

risks_watch: Further diesel increases beyond INR 8 could delay pass-through and compress margins, according to management.
Prolonged Gulf conflict may raise ATF prices, reduce air volumes and push costs up.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and social security norms, plus state-level pressure.
SME stress and the share of SME revenue, which fell to 48% to 52%.
Management has not disclosed non-surface volumes, which limits visibility on the rail and air business.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term recovery and margin path, but cautious on the near-term outlook. It repeatedly flagged the geopolitical risk, fuel and labour cost pressures and the SIR disruption, and it was evasive on non-surface volumes, which it declined to disclose.
